_doc: Code-testability ratings for NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3, HAND-AUTHORED, not from the standard. The AI 600-1 workbook ships NIST's own `code_testable` column; the 800-171 source does not rate testability at all, so this file supplies it and build-catalog.py joins it into controls.json by control id. Kept SEPARATE from controls.json for the same reason evidence-rules.json is: that file's contract is the standard's own text verbatim, and a rating we invented is our judgment, not NIST's. Changing a rating here is a deliberate, reviewable claim about what this engine can observe.

rubric.Yes: A detector's findings bear directly on the requirement; an empty finding bucket is real evidence the requirement is met in code.
rubric.Partial: Some code-observable component exists, but the requirement is materially broader than anything a scanner sees.
rubric.No: Organisational, physical, or personnel. Nothing a code scanner observes can evidence it. The evaluator forces these to `partial` with an explicit disclosure so they can never read as satisfied.

03.01.01.rationale: Auth wiring is visible in code; account creation/approval/notification lifecycle is a process no scanner observes.

03.01.02.rationale: Authorization enforcement is exactly what the broken-access-control, IDOR and framework-authz detectors decide.

03.01.03.rationale: SSRF, open-redirect and permissive CORS are real unintended-information-flow failures; network-layer flow control is not visible.

03.01.04.rationale: Separation of duties is an organisational role-design decision.

03.01.05.rationale: Over-broad RBAC bindings and IAM wildcards are least-privilege violations the IaC detectors decide directly.

03.01.06.rationale: Cluster-admin and wildcard IAM grants are observable; which humans hold privileged accounts is not.

03.01.07.rationale: Privilege-escalation paths are observable; logging of privileged-function execution is not.

03.01.08.rationale: Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints is directly detected.

03.01.09.rationale: Presence and wording of a system-use banner is a deployment/UI policy matter.

03.01.10.rationale: Device lock is an endpoint OS configuration.

03.01.11.rationale: Tokens issued without expiry are observable; server-side session termination policy is not.

03.01.12.rationale: Cleartext transport and disabled TLS verification are observable; VPN and remote-access authorization are not.

03.01.18.rationale: Insecure on-device storage and unsafe webviews are observable in mobile source; MDM enrollment and full-device encryption are not.

03.01.20.rationale: Authorization of external systems is a contractual and organisational control.

03.01.22.rationale: Publicly readable buckets are directly detected; whether the exposed content contains CUI requires human classification.

03.02.01.rationale: Security literacy training is delivered to people, not code.

03.02.02.rationale: Role-based training is delivered to people, not code.

03.03.01.rationale: No detector decides which event types a customer system logs; only the surrounding scan history is observable.

03.03.02.rationale: Audit record content fields are a logging-schema decision no detector inspects.

03.03.03.rationale: Audit record generation and retention are runtime properties this engine does not observe.

03.03.04.rationale: Alerting on audit-logging failure is an operational runbook control.

03.03.05.rationale: Human review and correlation of audit records.

03.03.06.rationale: Audit reduction and reporting is a SIEM capability.

03.03.07.rationale: System clock and timestamp granularity are host configuration.

03.03.08.rationale: This engine signs its own scan state (HMAC), which evidences integrity protection for its records only, not for the customer's audit store.

03.04.01.rationale: IaC misconfiguration findings bear on the declared baseline; whether it is under configuration control is a process.

03.04.02.rationale: Restrictive configuration settings are exactly what the IaC, Kubernetes, Terraform and Dockerfile detectors decide.

03.04.03.rationale: CI pipeline controls are observable; the change-approval process is not.

03.04.04.rationale: Scan history evidences that security impact was re-assessed after changes; the analysis itself is human.

03.04.05.rationale: Over-broad pipeline write permissions are observable; physical and logical change restrictions largely are not.

03.04.06.rationale: Broad container capabilities, host networking and root containers are precisely least-functionality violations.

03.04.08.rationale: Malicious and unexpected install scripts are detected; an allow-by-exception software inventory is not.

03.04.10.rationale: SBOM/AIBOM artifacts evidence a component inventory exists; their completeness is not verified by their existence.

03.04.11.rationale: Privacy taint output locates data flows; authoritative CUI location is a human determination.

03.04.12.rationale: Travel/high-risk-area device configuration is an operational control.

03.05.01.rationale: Unverified and forgeable tokens and missing authentication are directly detected.

03.05.03.rationale: No detector decides whether MFA is enforced for account access.

03.05.04.rationale: Tokens without expiry weaken replay resistance; nonce and challenge-response mechanisms are not decided.

03.05.05.rationale: Identifier assignment and reuse prevention is an identity-management process.

03.05.07.rationale: Weak password hashing and weak key derivation are directly detected.

03.05.11.rationale: Obscuring authentication feedback is a UI behaviour.

03.05.12.rationale: Hardcoded credentials and poor key hygiene are directly detected.

03.06.01.rationale: Incident handling is an operational capability.

03.06.02.rationale: Incident tracking and reporting is an operational process.

03.06.04.rationale: Incident response training is delivered to people.

03.06.05.rationale: The incident response plan is a document.

03.07.04.rationale: Maintenance tool control is a physical and operational process.

03.07.05.rationale: Nonlocal maintenance sessions are an operational control.

03.08.01.rationale: Media storage is a physical fact (a locked room, a controlled cabinet, an access-badged facility). Nothing about how CUI-bearing media is physically stored can be observed from source code or repository content.

03.08.02.rationale: Restricting who may physically handle media containing CUI is an access-control decision enforced by locks, custody logs and personnel, not by anything a code or configuration scanner reads.

03.08.03.rationale: Media sanitization is a physical disposal process.

03.08.04.rationale: Marking physical media (labels, handling caveats printed on a disk or drive) is a physical labeling practice with no corresponding artifact in source code, configuration, or a git repository.

03.08.05.rationale: Protecting and tracking media in transit outside a controlled area (chain-of-custody logs, transport containers, courier procedures) is a logistics and physical-security process this engine has no visibility into.

03.08.07.rationale: Removable media use restriction is an endpoint policy.

03.08.09.rationale: Encryption-disabled-at-rest findings bear on backup confidentiality; backup procedure and coverage are not observed.

03.09.01.rationale: Personnel screening (background checks prior to granting access, periodic rescreening) is an HR and vetting process conducted about people, entirely outside any code, configuration, or repository this engine reads.

03.09.02.rationale: Termination and transfer procedures are HR processes.

03.10.01.rationale: Physical facility access authorization (who may enter the building or room housing the system) is enforced by badges, guards and physical access-control hardware, none of which is observable from source code.

03.10.02.rationale: Monitoring physical access to a facility (camera footage, badge-swipe logs reviewed by security staff) is a physical-security operations activity with no code or repository artifact to inspect.

03.10.06.rationale: Security requirements for alternate work sites (home offices, temporary locations) are administrative and physical controls applied to a workspace, not something expressed in source code.

03.10.07.rationale: Physical access control at entry and exit points.

03.11.01.rationale: A generated threat model evidences that risk was assessed; the assessment's adequacy is human judgment.

03.11.02.rationale: Vulnerability scanning and dependency advisory monitoring is precisely what this engine does.

03.11.04.rationale: Fix history and triage records evidence response to findings; risk acceptance decisions are human.

03.12.01.rationale: Verifier runs and scan history evidence assessment activity; the formal assessment is broader.

03.12.02.rationale: Triage and fix-history records are a de facto POA&M; the formal plan is a document.

03.12.03.rationale: Watch mode and scan history evidence continuous monitoring of code; the wider strategy is organisational.

03.13.01.rationale: Host networking, permissive CORS, public buckets and SSRF are real boundary failures; firewalls and network segmentation are not visible.

03.13.04.rationale: Data-exposure findings bear on unintended transfer via shared resources; memory and resource reuse at the OS level is not observed.

03.13.06.rationale: Wildcard and host-network configurations contradict deny-by-default; the network default posture itself is infrastructure.

03.13.08.rationale: Cleartext transport, weak TLS, disabled certificate verification and encryption-disabled-at-rest are directly detected.

03.13.09.rationale: Missing token expiry bears on session termination; network-level disconnect is not observed.

03.13.10.rationale: Hardcoded keys, inline RPC keys, static IVs and poor key hygiene are directly detected.

03.13.11.rationale: Weak ciphers, weak hashes, ECB mode, weak KDFs and quantum-vulnerable primitives are directly detected.

03.13.12.rationale: Collaborative computing device activation is an endpoint control.

03.13.13.rationale: Unsafe client-side execution and unsanitized HTML rendering are mobile-code risks; organisational mobile-code policy is not observed.

03.13.15.rationale: Insecure session cookies, missing CSRF protection and disabled TLS verification are directly detected.

03.14.01.rationale: Identifying and correcting system flaws is the engine's primary function, with fix history as corroboration.

03.14.02.rationale: Malicious install scripts and supply-chain findings are detected; runtime antimalware is not observed.

03.14.03.rationale: The CVE alert daemon evidences receipt of external advisories; internal dissemination is a process.

03.14.06.rationale: Watch mode and scan history evidence code monitoring; network and host intrusion monitoring is not observed.

03.14.08.rationale: Privacy taint output bears on where CUI is handled; retention policy compliance is organisational.

03.15.01.rationale: A committed compliance policy artifact evidences documented procedures; dissemination and review are process.

03.15.02.rationale: A System Security Plan is a written document describing the system's components, boundaries, threats and safeguards. Its existence and content are authored and reviewed by people; this engine can generate supporting artifacts (a threat model, an SBOM) but does not produce or verify the SSP document itself.

03.15.03.rationale: Rules of behaviour are acknowledged by people.

03.16.01.rationale: A generated threat model evidences security engineering activity; principle application is human judgment.

03.16.02.rationale: End-of-life base images and unsupported dependencies are directly detected.

03.16.03.rationale: External service provider requirements are contractual.

03.17.01.rationale: SBOM history evidences supply-chain visibility; the SCRM plan is a document.

03.17.02.rationale: License attribution and SBOM artifacts bear on acquisition practice; procurement strategy is organisational.

03.17.03.rationale: Supply-chain weaknesses, malicious packages and provenance verification are directly detected.
